about: The short state of the work between the orchestrator and the GPU worker. Read it first after any restart; docs/PIPELINE.md says how the two work. Only the orchestrator edits it. A goal is open until the worker has confirmed the outcome on real hardware, then closed; it is with_owner when three rounds did not settle it or the decision is the owner's to make.

goals.name: The memory step
goals.decides: Which line Setup shows for a graphics card smaller than the model, and for which cards
goals.so_far: Settled: --diffusion-fa is what the engine needs on any card; the two option sets fail alike on one piece; and the engine's --max-vram 8 cures the one-piece failure for the standard model on a 12 GB card (WO-03: 5 of 5 with a gigabyte held, 5 of 5 on the published site straight after the saved options failed 5 in 8, same seconds). Round 2: Setup's line for Flux-2-Klein-4B on a 12 to 16 GB card is now --diffusion-fa --offload-to-cpu --max-vram 8, and someone with only the first two saved is shown the step again with its reason. No other card or model is given the option, since none was measured. WO-04 confirms it on the published site; this is the second of three rounds. To weigh afterwards: with --offload-to-cpu the whole model sits in ordinary memory (15.2 GB standard, 17.6 GB larger), which a 16 GB computer may not have.

goals.name: Knowing the step is done
goals.decides: Which field of the app's model list shows the saved options, so Setup can put the step away
goals.outcome: WO-02 confirmed it on the published site against the real app: the step is hidden for a model with --diffusion-fa saved, shown for one without under every kind of computer, and gone once its line has been run and Connect pressed. The app's real model-list entry is pinned in test/local.test.js.

goals.name: The download readout
goals.decides: Whether Setup's size, speed and time left match the app's own window
goals.outcome: WO-01: the readout matched the app's own window at three points on a 19.3 GB download (the window counts in 1024s and labels them GB and MB/s; the page counts in decimal GB and megabits a second). Nothing in the page changed for it.

goals.name: What a local model keeps
goals.decides: How many pieces it keeps faithfully, and what Setup and the README should promise
goals.outcome: WO-01: with four pieces or fewer no piece was missing in 18 different pictures, so the cap stays at four. Exactness suffers instead (lettering redrawn by the smaller model, odd shapes made ordinary, a hat's colour shifted, jewellery added); the README now says so.

goals.name: The larger model
goals.decides: Whether Flux-2-Klein-9B-GGUF is worth suggesting, and for which cards
goals.outcome: WO-01 measured it on a 12 GB card: Flux-2-Klein-9B-GGUF ran with --diffusion-fa, took about one and a half times as long, and kept a lettered print right where the smaller model garbled it. The owner's answer (2026-11-26) was that quality is the priority, so Setup suggests the larger model from 12 GB up, uses a model that is already downloaded before asking for a 19 GB download, and tells someone on the standard model that the larger one keeps prints better. Not measured: a 16 GB computer, where the larger model's files may not fit in ordinary memory with --offload-to-cpu.

goals.name: A new picture each time
goals.decides: Whether making the same outfit again on a local model gives a different picture
goals.outcome: WO-02 confirmed it on the published site: three requests for one outfit gave three files, three seeds in the engine's log and three pictures that differ to the eye.

goals.name: Bottoms added to a lone top
goals.decides: Whether naming the added pieces outright stops a local model inventing malformed bottoms
goals.outcome: WO-03 confirmed it on the published site and in the checkout: with the instruction naming the added pieces, 28 one-piece pictures in 28 (24 from the standard model, 4 from the larger) showed whole, plain, full-length trousers and plain shoes, against 4 malformed in 11 before.

in_flight.with: the worker on the owner's computer

next: The download readout between two files: the app reports no progress for about half a minute and the page then shows the size alone, which reads as stuck. It can only be confirmed during a real download, so it waits for the next one.
Setup, 'What kind of computer is this?': choosing 'Choose…' by hand shows the advice for the page's own guess (WO-02, surprise 6). Small; fix with the next change to Setup.

A shorter instruction for local models: they lost odd shapes (the clown shoes in every picture) and sometimes added jewellery. Naming the added pieces outright fixed the bottoms, so plainer, more literal wording may help here too. A work order after WO-04.
--max-vram for cards that were not measured: an 11 GB card is likely the most fragile of all, and nothing is known for 8, 16 or 24 GB. Needs other hardware, which the worker does not have.
dead_ends: --offload-to-cpu on its own as the memory step: on a 12 GB card it failed every outfit of two to four pieces, exactly as no options did (WO-01).
"Try again with fewer pieces" as advice for a failed local picture: with the card nearly full, one piece was the outfit that failed and adding a second made it work (WO-01).
Choosing between --diffusion-fa alone and both options to make a one-piece outfit safer: with part of the card held they fail alike, for the same stated reason (WO-02).
--max-vram -1 (reserve a gigabyte of whatever is free): the engine works the figure out once at load and still plans one block; 2 of 5 with a gigabyte held (WO-03).
--max-vram 6: it works, but every picture's last stage fails once and is redone in tiles (WO-03). 8 leaves that stage alone.
owner_priorities: 2026-11-26: quality is the priority. Where faithfulness to the pieces trades against speed, download size or a few cents, choose faithfulness (CLAUDE.md, Rules).
for_the_owner: WO-02, surprise 7: the worker started LM Studio's background service by mistake (it ran LM Studio's command-line tool to list models) and its attempt to close it was refused. It is still running on the owner's computer; quitting LM Studio closes it.
